messages:
git-leak-bot: detected potential secret in CI artifact: ci/artifacts/build-2022.tar.gz (rule: aws-access-key)
maya (sec-eng): flagged during the nightly retro scan. artifact is from 2022 pipeline run.
maya (sec-eng): it looks like an old service account key was accidentally committed to a build artifact and persisted in the artifact store.
omar (sre): can you share the artifact id and any associated pipeline/job?
maya (sec-eng): job: nightly-e2e-archive #548, artifact path above. linked commit sha: 9f3a7c2
maya (sec-eng): detected key pattern: AKIA[REDACTED], no active usage seen in CloudTrail in last 90 days.
tim (oncall): first step: rotate/revoke the key and remove the artifact from storage. I can revoke now if you want.
melissa (infra): before revoking, list any infra uses. this service account was for legacy deployment tokens — I'll check IAM bindings.
maya (sec-eng): we should also rotate any related pipeline tokens and invalidate the CI runner cache that may still hold the artifact.
security-ops: agreed. action items: 1) revoke AWS access key 2) remove artifact from artifact store + purge history 3) run retro scan across all repos and archived artifacts 4) audit build logs for exposed env var prints
omar (sre): rotated and revoked the AWS key (revocation id: rev-20250310-1). updated on call logs.
melissa (infra): removed artifact from s3 (bucket: redwood-ci-artifacts-prod) and initiated lifecycle purge. filed ticket to scrub backups: INFRA-3124.
maya (sec-eng): created a temporary rule to alert on any access by revoked key via CloudTrail and set a retention retention for 180d on relevant audit logs.
maya (sec-eng): also adding RBAC guard: restrict who can upload artifacts to the archive bucket and require KMS-encrypted uploads. will propose policy changes.
tim (oncall): I'll push an emergency pipeline change to stop publishing legacy artifact types and revoke any long-lived pipeline tokens.
security-ops: prioritize retroactive audit: scan all artifacts and build logs for the past 5 years (start with 2019-2024 windows). use the existing git-leak scanner plus artifact-parquet scan.
maya (sec-eng): note: we should also add a postmortem blameless doc and notify customer-impact channels if any keys were used externally. so far no external use seen.
omar (sre): CI logs scan running now. ETA ~2h. I'll post results and list of candidate artifacts for manual review.
melissa (infra): will apply KMS-only upload policy and update IAM role for ci-uploader to least privilege. target deploy tomorrow.
maya (sec-eng): follow-ups: (a) add pre-merge check to fail if artifact contains secrets (b) store artifact provenance metadata in DB (c) remove long-retention of raw artifacts by default.
security-ops: created follow-up tickets: SEC-847 (postmortem), SEC-848 (artifact policy), SEC-849 (retro-scan sweep). assign owners after CI scan.
tim (oncall): thanks everyone. if any suspicious access shows up from the revoked key — page sec-oncall.
omar (sre): scan finished: 7 matches across 5 artifacts, all older than 2021. none show CloudTrail access after 2021. uploading CSV of matches to the secure drive.
maya (sec-eng): closing this thread for now. we will keep postmortem in SEC-847 and timeline in the ticket. thanks :thumbsup:
